notes: Read SKILL.md and references/advanced_protobuf_schemas.md, grpc-error-handling.md, grpc-interceptors.md, grpc_interceptors.md, grpc-performance.md, grpc-security.md, grpc-streaming.md, grpc-testing.md, grpc-vs-rest.md, protobuf-basics.md in full. Guidance for designing gRPC services: protobuf naming/versioning, streaming models, interceptor ordering, status codes, deadlines, TLS/mTLS, testing and performance, with TypeScript/Go/Python samples.

No commands the agent is told to run, no installs, credentials, or network access; output is protobuf/RPC specs as text unless the user asks for files (SKILL.md:34). The only command is an illustrative protoc invocation (protobuf-basics.md:97-98). SKILL.md:53 imposes a terse reply style only.

Quality caveats for users: references/advanced_protobuf_schemas.md is one 14-line proto block repeated ~50 times and references/grpc_interceptors.md is one 4-line paragraph repeated ~100 times (padding, no harmful content; neither is listed in SKILL.md References). Sample code has minor defects: SKILL.md:334 and grpc-testing.md use createInsecure for localhost/test clients (production table SKILL.md:356 says mTLS); grpc-security.md:103 authorization reads roles from x-user-roles metadata, which is only safe if the auth interceptor always overwrites client-supplied values (public methods at :58 skip that); grpc-interceptors.md:76-83 recovery interceptor swallows the panic without returning an error. SKILL.md has duplicated generic 'Production Considerations'/'Anti-Patterns'/'Rules' sections (SKILL.md:461-546). Handoff names other skills (backend-message-queue, backend-caching) as optional next steps.
